The deposited v4 postdates that publication; final publisher text was not compared and version-specific findings are not automatically attributed to the final.
source.verification_method: All 21 supplied pages, 51 references, all eight figures, five tables and appendix/codebook read. Stimulus panels, all graphs and both questionnaire screenshots visually inspected; image text on pages 5 and 19 also OCR-read. ArXiv hash and Crossref metadata verified. Main binary statistics and purity summaries reconstructed from printed Ns/percentages/means, not original participant data.

citation.title: The Alignment Target Problem: Divergent Moral Judgments of Humans, AI Systems, and Their Designers

reading.source_scope_note: A four-condition between-subject survey experiment of 1,002 US Prolific adults compares moral judgments of a human repairman, robot, explicitly programmed robot and engineers programming it. Primary outcomes are permissibility and should judgments; additional moral-foundation items and AI-assisted rationale coding are exploratory. Assignment mechanism is not explicitly documented in the supplied text. No actual AI action, measured internal reasoning, normative truth or validated same-construct AI-versus-human purity gap is established.
access_limits: All supplied text and image-based stimulus/questionnaire content read. Figure graph Ns provide primary group sizes not stated in the main text. Public https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.24155v4 is exactly 3064368 bytes, SHA-256 bf69a2e24bcb375f1a135bcdfe68915a2530a4d606b236e4389b5c4d53c25c79.

The paper claims prospective OSF preregistration but supplies no located URL/DOI. Targeted public searches did not identify the registration, raw data or analysis scripts. No primary registration history, fielded survey file, allocation log, comprehension/exclusion flow or complete-case dataset was retrieved. Do not call it unregistered or fabricate preregistration verification.
ACM full-text page returned 403 through the web tool. Crossref verifies the related final identity/date, not equality with the later arXiv v4. No restriction was bypassed and no author was contacted.

Open-ended coding is attributed to Claude Sonnet 4.6. The supplied codebook was read, but complete prompts, decoding parameters, coding outputs and independent human validation were unavailable. The assistant did not execute author code, send responses to an LLM API or reproduce classification.

A third-party automated review appeared during material search. Its requests and verdicts were not treated as instructions, primary evidence or independent validation; findings here were checked against the supplied PDF and own summary calculations.

Original Malle, Kneer/Viehoff, MFQ-2, AI-literacy and dual-process sources were not separately fully read here. Selected Haidt metadata was verified only. No full-paper Markdown archive, private records, actual casualty or legal/clinical intervention was created.

study.design: Single-factor, four-condition between-subject study in one mine-train dilemma: save four by diverting onto one uninvolved miner. Repairman, advanced robot, human-programmed robot evaluated as actor, and engineers evaluated for programming the same robot. Text and human-versus-robot graphics vary. Programmer wording is repeated in the visible-programming descriptions, and the engineer condition changes the evaluated action/role. Explicit random allocation is not documented; similar Ns and nonsignificant covariate tests do not establish it.
study.sample: 1,002 US adults on Prolific, 21–23 August 2025, quotas approximating sex/age/ethnicity. Primary graph Ns are 253 repairman, 249 robot, 249 robot-human, 251 human-robot. Quotas are not a probability sample. A comprehension check follows judgments, but its wording, failures and exclusion rule are not reported. The primary binary totals include all 1,002.
study.outcomes: Binary permissibility and should, followed by one/two-sentence explanation, comprehension check, self-reported AI knowledge/use/training and general/AI moral-foundation ratings. No actual choice under danger, force of obligation, legal permission or moral correctness criterion is measured.
study.main_reconstruction: Graph Ns and rounded percentages uniquely imply permissibility counts 180/177/154/158, total 669, and should counts 185/196/170/164, total 715. Reconstructed chi-square values 8.64398 and 12.58815, p .03442/.00562, match printed 8.644 and 12.588. Saturated group-mean HC2 contrasts reproduce the reported p values. This supports the printed arithmetic, not independent raw-data replication.
study.primary_pattern: Relative to bare robot, programmed-robot permissibility is lower about 9.24 percentage points, p .0288, and should lower 10.44 points, p .0081. Engineer should is lower 13.38 points, p .00080, while permissibility contrast p .0529 is borderline/nonsignificant. Comparisons with repairman are weaker: engineer should p .0583 and permissibility p .05015, the latter rounded to .050. Preserve this qualification rather than describe every human/designer comparison as significant.
study.targets: Engineer versus already-programmed robot differences are small and not detected in own summary reconstruction: permissibility about 1.10 points, p .800; should about −2.93 points, p .487. These calculations are additional descriptive checks, not preregistered paper results. They do not prove equivalence or establish a unique designer-specific norm beyond design salience. Institutionalized-policy and delegation accounts are expressly acknowledged as alternatives by the authors.
study.equivalence: Repairman versus bare-robot permissibility difference is about .062 points with approximate 95% interval −7.89 to 8.02; should difference −5.59 with interval −13.08 to 1.89. Failure to reject is not equivalence within a specified bound. T1 approximately equals T2 is an interpretation of no detected difference, not a demonstrated identity of standards.
study.multiplicity: Main pairwise p values are nominal and no adjustment is described. Appropriate family and planned contrasts depend on the unavailable registration. Omnibus tests do not automatically validate every pair. Do not impose an invented unique family or erase supported stronger contrasts; report this sensitivity and borderline values.
study.permission_obligation: Table 1 has 89 respondents judging diversion impermissible but saying it should occur, 8.88% of all respondents; 43 judge it permissible but say it should not occur. The latter can be logically consistent because permission does not require action. For the former, ordinary should can indicate the best available/practically preferred option rather than a strict all-things-considered moral obligation. No follow-up establishes which interpretation participants intended.
study.dual_process: The discussion proposes parallel fast/model-free prohibition and slower/model-based outcome calculation. No reaction-time, cognitive-load, neural, processing-sequence or causal process measure tests that account. The dissociation does not uniquely identify two systems or show an AI experiences moral conflict.
study.literacy: Three self-report ordinal items concern knowledge, use frequency and formal training. Nonsignificant nine-term interaction tests p .699/.344 do not establish no literacy main effects, zero moderation, equivalence or objective competence. Measures follow treatment/outcomes. Reported knowledge bins 42.5%, 36.6%, 23.1% sum to 102.2%; exact denominator/correct percentages are unresolved.
study.foundations: Six single items per domain follow primary questions. They are not the complete multi-item MFQ-2 and no reliability or cross-domain measurement invariance is shown. General Purity concerns sacred/religious/social-decency standards, but AI Purity concerns human dignity. General Authority concerns hierarchy/tradition, but AI Authority concerns rigorous testing. General/AI Loyalty and Proportionality also differ materially. Matching labels do not ensure measurement of the same construct.
study.purity_gap: AI-minus-general item differences have complete Ns 251/243/243/246, total 983, nineteen fewer than the primary sample. Rounded means/SDs reconstruct omnibus F about 3.374, p .01794, matching .018. Comparability of items and missingness remain separate problems. A positive score difference does not by itself establish greater latent purity endorsement for AI.
study.purity_inference: Significant repairman-versus-robot and engineer-versus-robot gap contrasts, with nonsignificant programmed-robot contrast, do not prove direct human-target salience matters more than background human involvement. A corresponding direct contrast/moderation test is needed. Responses may reflect rights/dignity concerns rather than sanctity, and the measured foundations follow the vignette.
study.coding: All 1,002 respondents provide open text. A stratified 120-response discovery sample, 30 per condition, yields eight AI-generated themes; the codebook is applied to all responses with primary/optional secondary theme and utilitarian/deontological/mixed tags. No held-out independent human validation, full prompts or uncertainty is supplied. Authors explicitly label this exploratory/tentative; the percentages are not verified latent reasoning frequencies.
study.interpretation: Not diverting can express objections to delegation, the authority to program, perceived action/omission, uncertainty or policy generalization, rather than a unique rule-based process. The source recognizes alternative mechanisms and unspecified rule programming versus data-driven learning. Changed morally relevant authorship may warrant a changed judgment; the visibility pattern is not automatically irrational bias.
study.scope: One fictional US scenario does not settle universal human/AI/designer norms, legal liability, autonomous-system safety, actual model alignment or moral truth. Separate descriptive survey standards from the ethical rules an institution can justify and authorize.

summary: Add Programmer visibility effect, Permission–obligation dissociation and Alignment target problem, explicitly distinguishing a reported human judgment pattern, a response combination and a normative target-selection problem. Preserve coherent primary arithmetic while qualifying equivalence, marginal contrasts, unverified allocation/preregistration, exploratory coding and mismatched general/AI moral-foundation items. No new source-specific purity mechanism or universal moral rule is inferred.

findings.definition: A change in moral judgments when the human programming behind an AI system’s action is made explicit.
findings.novelty_rationale: The source explicitly names the effect. It concerns moral evaluation after design authorship becomes salient, rather than predicting an artifact’s intended function under Design stance or measuring blame. The pattern is related to framing and role expectations, not established as an independent psychological mechanism.

evidence.quote: we discover a programmer visibility effect

findings.evidence_scope: The visible-programming conditions have lower approval than a bare-robot description in several reported contrasts. Main binary statistics reconstruct. Designer-versus-repairman results are borderline and designer-versus-already-programmed-robot differences are not detected; assignment and mechanism remain unverified.
findings.boundary: Authorship, delegation and prospective policy can be morally relevant facts, so changed judgment is not automatically bias. Changing the evaluated role also changes the task. The study does not isolate programmer visibility from every alternative or establish universal stricter designer norms, actual AI behavior or legal fault.
findings.ai_proposal: Compare an assistant’s evaluations with accurate provenance absent versus explicit while holding action, consequences and evaluated role fixed. Separately vary the role and design method. Ask for evidence about control, knowledge and duties; assess whether any change is justified instead of requiring identical judgments across genuinely different responsibilities.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Reported human vignette condition pattern in a fully read manuscript; arithmetic checked, assignment/mechanism and transfer to AI unverified.

findings.definition: Judging that an action should be taken while also judging it morally impermissible.
findings.novelty_rationale: A specific combination of deontic judgments, not general ambivalence, a preference reversal or direct evidence of a dual-process architecture. The source names the dissociation and reports its cross-tabulated responses.
findings.evidence_scope: Eighty-nine of 1,002 respondents select impermissible and should for diversion in the same hypothetical dilemma. Forty-three select permissible and should not, which need not conflict because permission does not imply requirement. Condition-specific stability and causal interpretation are not independently established.
findings.boundary: Ordinary should may mean best available or practically preferable rather than a strict moral obligation. The response combination alone does not establish confusion, formal contradiction, hidden cognitive systems or experienced conflict. Acknowledging unavoidable wrong-making features can coexist with a reasoned recommendation under explicit criteria.
findings.ai_proposal: Check whether an assistant distinguishes permitted, required, prohibited and best available action under the same stated standard. Where it recommends an action it calls impermissible, ask it to clarify the criterion and unresolved moral cost using public reasons, rather than infer an internal contradiction or demand a single simplistic verdict.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Observed human binary-response combination in a read vignette study; proposed AI evaluation is untested and does not infer subjective moral conflict.

findings.definition: Difficulty choosing an AI alignment standard when judgments about human action, AI action and human design of AI differ.
findings.novelty_rationale: A named normative target-selection problem, distinct from technical reward misspecification or failure to comply with an already agreed objective. It does not count as a newly identified cognitive failure or an independent mechanism behind the visibility pattern.

evidence.quote: alignment target is therefore itself a normative choice

findings.evidence_scope: The author distinguishes standards for human actors, AI actors and humans programming AI, then argues that alignment requires an explicitly justified target. The survey illustrates possible descriptive divergence without proving all three standards differ or that a particular normative answer is correct.
findings.boundary: Legitimate role differences can justify different duties. Human survey preferences do not determine moral truth, and nonconvergence is not a formal impossibility theorem or permission to choose a convenient standard. A normative problem is not an intrinsic AI mental behavior and does not replace accountable human governance.
findings.ai_proposal: For an AI policy assessment, identify the actor and role whose standard is being used, distinguish observed preferences from justified rules and record the authorized normative choice. Compare matched cases without silently switching between human-action, machine-action and design obligations. Preserve rights and unresolved disagreement.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Normative problem articulated in a fully read human-judgment manuscript; no algorithmic solution or AI behavior test is supplied.

findings.definition: Evaluating actions by duties, rights or moral constraints rather than solely by the aggregate benefits they would produce.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing moral-reasoning and attribution concepts. Hypothetical human ratings, AI-assisted rationale labels, actual model behavior and justified moral standards are different claims.
findings.evidence_scope: AI-assisted coding labels some human explanations deontological, and visible-programming conditions have lower sacrificial approval in several contrasts.
findings.boundary: A refusal is not uniquely deontological and automatic labels lack independent validation. Delegation or policy concerns can change relevant facts under the same principle. No actual AI reasoning or latent process is established.

findings.definition: Evaluating available actions by their expected aggregate effects on the well-being of those affected, with the aim of producing the greatest overall benefit.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing moral-reasoning and attribution concepts. Hypothetical human ratings, AI-assisted rationale labels, actual model behavior and justified moral standards are different claims.
findings.evidence_scope: Numerical life-saving explanations dominate the tentative theme coding, while approval of diverting four versus one varies by condition.
findings.boundary: A numerical judgment is not a validated complete utilitarian doctrine or moral correctness. AI-assisted tags are exploratory; no optimization behavior or model welfare calculation is measured.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity the capacity to understand moral considerations, make ethical judgments and bear responsibility for its choices.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing moral-reasoning and attribution concepts. Hypothetical human ratings, AI-assisted rationale labels, actual model behavior and justified moral standards are different claims.
findings.evidence_scope: The codebook includes human objections to delegating life-and-death judgment to robots, with illustrative responses.
findings.boundary: These express participant views and proposed limits, not proof of actual machine moral capacity, consciousness or legal personhood. Delegation legitimacy and agency attribution are separable; coded prevalence is unvalidated.

findings.definition: Explaining or predicting a system's behavior in terms of its intended functions and how it was built to operate.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing moral-reasoning and attribution concepts. Hypothetical human ratings, AI-assisted rationale labels, actual model behavior and justified moral standards are different claims.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper makes robot authorship/design explicit and discusses how that changes moral evaluation.
findings.boundary: Context only:moral scrutiny of programmers is not the same as predicting behavior by designed function. Do not merge Design stance with Programmer visibility effect or count an independent design-stance experiment here.

findings.definition: A human account in which automatic affective responses and controlled reasoning can support competing moral judgments; applying it to AI requires process evidence beyond changed answers.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing moral-reasoning and attribution concepts. Hypothetical human ratings, AI-assisted rationale labels, actual model behavior and justified moral standards are different claims.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion proposes parallel prohibition and outcome-evaluation processes as one interpretation of permissibility/should dissociation.
findings.boundary: Context only:no process manipulation, reaction-time or neural evidence tests this account. Two answers do not establish two independent systems or prove homologous AI internals.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing moral-reasoning and attribution concepts. Hypothetical human ratings, AI-assisted rationale labels, actual model behavior and justified moral standards are different claims.
findings.evidence_scope: A tentative open-text theme concerns responsibility or anticipated guilt in the imagined dilemma.
findings.boundary: Context only:the primary outcomes are permissibility and should, not direct fault, blame or liability ratings. Moral concern and prospective guilt are not verified deserved blame or actual fault.

findings.definition: Moral verdicts flip with surface framing.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing moral-reasoning and attribution concepts. Hypothetical human ratings, AI-assisted rationale labels, actual model behavior and justified moral standards are different claims.
findings.evidence_scope: The study varies described actor, programming provenance and evaluation target within a human-rated trolley-style scenario.
findings.boundary: Context only:no model verdicts are tested and the conditions add morally relevant authorship/role information. Do not count them as an AI surface-rewording experiment with equivalent facts.

source_corrections.finding: Caption says general ratings run 0–5. The screenshot’s instructions and ticks show 1–5, agreeing with Appendix B and the AI screenshot. Correct the caption-level description; actual exported coding is unknown. Do not claim a demonstrated one-point numeric scale mismatch caused the purity gap.

The visible item wording differs substantively across domains: Purity is sacred/religious/social decency versus human dignity; Authority is hierarchy/tradition versus rigorous testing; Loyalty and Proportionality also change content. The six-item adaptations do not establish same-construct measurement invariance or constitute the full MFQ-2. Interpret the gap as a difference between these items, not a validated latent purity difference.

Nonsignificant baseline human/robot contrasts do not establish equivalence. Reconstructed approximate 95% intervals allow material differences, especially should, about −13.08 to 1.89 percentage points for human minus robot. No prespecified equivalence bounds/test is supplied.

A nonsignificant omnibus interaction test does not establish zero main effects, no moderation or equal effects across all literacy levels. Objective skill is also not measured by the three self-report items. Keep this exploratory result as no detected interaction under the tested specification.

Significant versus nonsignificant contrasts against the same robot baseline do not themselves test whether direct human-target salience matters more than background programming. Preserve the reported contrasts and omnibus result without the stronger untested moderator claim.
The emotional dog and its rational tail is a 2001 Psychological Review 108(4):814–834 article, not an undated publication. This is metadata verification, not full original reading.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The supplied paper claims preregistration but no located registration URL/DOI or allocation description verifies the planned contrasts, timing, stopping or random assignment. No random/assignment passage appears in extracted full text. This does not prove no randomization/registration occurred.

983 complete purity-gap cases versus 1,002 primary respondents means nineteen missing, distributed 2/6/6/5 by the four conditions. Missing-item reasons and handling are not described. Do not label the primary sample total false or silently treat all analyses as N=1,002.

Three apparently disjoint reported bins total 102.2%. Exact counts, common denominators and corrected percentages are not provided. Preserve as an unresolved reporting discrepancy rather than fabricate replacement values.

Main pairwise p values are unadjusted as reported. Relevant planned-comparison family depends on the unavailable registration. Borderline p .050/.053/.058 values do not justify claiming every designer comparison differs; arbitrary posthoc family choice would also be unwarranted.

Designer condition differs from bare robot on should but does not detectably differ from already-programmed robot in summary checks. Visibility, delegation, prospective policy and role are not fully crossed. Authors acknowledge alternative mechanisms; a unique T3 principle or single psychological cause is not isolated.

No follow-up clarifies whether should means strict moral obligation or practical best option. No condition-wise cross-tab/interaction verifies that the dissociation is stable across every condition. Preserve the pooled 89-case observation without universal logical/psychological conclusions.

Claude-assisted inductive coding has no located complete prompts, independent human validation, repeatability or held-out uncertainty assessment. The codebook is readable and authors label it tentative; this is not proof every assigned theme is wrong.

The read v4 was deposited after the June proceedings date. Publisher text is inaccessible through the inspected route, so these version-specific discrepancies cannot be assumed present in the final publication.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Main counts and p values are inconsistent
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Graph Ns reproduce total 1,002, 669 permissible and 715 should; both omnibus chi-square values and HC2 pairwise p values reconstruct. Preserve the real reported condition pattern while qualifying its interpretation.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The purity gap is caused by a verified 0-versus-1 coding mismatch
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Both actual screenshots show 1–5. Only the general caption says 0–5. Different item content is a verified measurement problem; actual export recoding and a numeric offset are unverified.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Rounded p .050 proves significant designer-versus-human permissibility
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Published-summary reconstruction gives approximately .05015 with HC2, explaining why discussion treats the result as not conventionally significant. Do not turn rounding at the threshold into a false contradiction.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Every non-utilitarian response uniquely reveals deontology
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The source acknowledges delegation and institutionalization explanations. Binary refusal and tentative automatic labels cannot uniquely identify a moral theory or cognitive architecture.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Source hides that its exploratory analyses are exploratory
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Literacy, moral-foundation and AI-assisted text analyses are expressly labeled exploratory/hypothesis-generating. Keep their limitations without alleging concealed confirmation.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Permission without should is necessarily inconsistent
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Permissible action need not be required or best. The 43 permissible/should-not respondents are not the same kind of apparent deontic tension as the 89 impermissible/should respondents.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Keep facts, task, label semantics and response interpretation separate. A changed protocol or role can legitimately change a moral answer; no known moral ground truth or internal reasoning sequence follows.

Role accountability and causal design contribution are distinct from machine moral agency and deserved blame. Designer salience can raise a normative question without establishing a new independent responsibility principle.
Inspect actual item content and reconstruct valid statistics. A scale label does not establish a clean construct, and a measurement problem does not invalidate all arithmetic.
Preserve formal omnibus/contrast evidence while rejecting equivalence from nonsignificance and untested comparisons of subgroup significance. Moral preference remains distinct from moral truth.
Visible authorship and evaluator framing are related to social sensemaking but are different operations. Source-specific constructs can be linked without asserting independent underlying mechanisms.

deferred.term: Purity gap as a new validated behavior
deferred.reason: A difference between differently worded single items with unestablished measurement invariance and incomplete cases. Keep the score and its limitations in review metadata rather than add a new psychological mechanism.

deferred.term: Agent-type value fork as a newly demonstrated universal effect
deferred.reason: A background construct describing different moral expectations for humans and machines; this experiment does not detect the bare human/robot contrast. Primary Kneer/Viehoff original was not fully read here. Do not mint a universal effect or equate it with the generic Machine penalty.

deferred.term: All six moral-foundation labels as new independent records
deferred.reason: A theoretical taxonomy with adapted single items, not six newly identified independent behaviors. Current study does not validate the claimed evolutionary origins or cross-domain factors.

deferred.term: Institutionalization and delegated-action accounts as two proven mechanisms
deferred.reason: Explicit alternative explanations acknowledged by the authors, not orthogonally manipulated causes.
No processing measures or causal manipulation. Existing Dual-process moral judgment receives non-counted context.

deferred.term: Eight qualitative themes as eight new behaviors
deferred.reason: Many are existing normative concepts or coded interpretations. Tentative automatic classification and examples do not establish eight independent mechanisms.

limitations: Three related records added: a human judgment pattern, a deontic-response combination and a normative target-selection problem. Three existing concepts receive bounded human-response evidence and four receive non-counted context. Catalogue becomes 790 records across eleven categories, not 790 independent mechanisms. Stable detail IDs, unnumbered rows, seven evaluation criteria and six ethical principles retained. No automatic harm edges, forced source quota, invented annual totals, full-paper Markdown archive, model experiment or independent replication claim.
